title: STAHN Security Alert Event
description: Frozen cross-layer alert contract for Phase 1 detection and Phase 2 evidence logging. Every field listed here corresponds to a field named in Research Objective 2 ('the interface between the two layers is a frozen alert contract'). Field order below is normative for canonical serialisation; see docs/canonicalisation_spec.md.

contract_version.description: Version of this frozen alert contract. A consumer must reject any event whose contract_version it does not recognise rather than guess at field semantics.

event_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this detection event, assigned once by the detection agent at emission time and never reused.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the detection event, e.g. 2026-09-15T18:04:12.501Z.

verdict.description: Binary classification verdict emitted by the detection layer.

threat_category.description: Coarse threat category. Objective 1 defines seven coarse categories collapsed from fifteen fine-grained labels on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2; this contract additionally admits the CICIoT2023 coarse families actually emitted by the deployed Phase 1 STAHN artifact so the schema is truthful about both the registered detection layer and the delivered one. 'Other' is used only when the emitting model cannot resolve a finer category (e.g. a binary-only classifier).

severity.description: Operational severity derived from threat_category and calibrated_confidence by the anchoring policy (config/anchoring-policy.example.yaml).

calibrated_confidence.description: Calibrated confidence score in [0,1]. Objective 1 fits isotonic calibration on the validation fold before this score is produced; the anchoring gate of Objective 3 is only defensible against a calibrated score. This contract carries a `calibration` sub-object (see below) so a downstream auditor can tell a calibrated score from a raw, uncalibrated model output.

is_calibrated.description: False when the emitting detection layer has not fitted a calibrator (e.g. the delivered Phase 1 STAHN artifact, which reports raw softmax output). The anchoring policy must widen its safety margin when this is false.

method.description: Calibration method applied, or 'none' if calibrated_confidence is a raw model score.

source_address.description: Source IP:port, carried as nullable alert metadata only. Objective 1 deliberately excludes identifiers from the feature space; they travel here so an analyst can act on an alert without the model having trained on them.

destination_address.description: Destination IP:port, carried as nullable alert metadata only, for the same reason as source_address.

resource_id.description: Derived cloud resource identifier (e.g. instance ID, container ID, or interface ID) that observed the flow.

triggering_features.description: The feature vector consumed by the model for this flow, keyed by feature name. Carried so an auditor can recompute the verdict independently of the live model service.

model_id.description: Stable logical identifier for the deployed model family, e.g. 'stahn-phase1'.

model_digest.description: SHA-256 digest computed over every prediction-affecting component of the deployed artifact (serialised model, feature ordering, label ordering, hyperparameters, thresholds). See src/model_provenance.py. This digest is anchored on-chain once per retraining cycle (contracts/model_provenance.schema.json) and referenced by every alert produced under that model.

feature_attributions.description: Ranked per-feature attributions for this verdict (e.g. SHAP values), most influential first. May be empty for a model family that does not yet supply attributions.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of this event's canonical serialisation (docs/canonicalisation_spec.md), computed over every field except payload_digest itself. This is the value committed to the ledger and independently recomputed by an auditor.

inference_latency_ms.description: Measured wall-clock inference latency in milliseconds for this single flow.
